descriptions.name: wide_fm_tone
descriptions.description: Warbird-like dive pass, 4th harmonic dominant (812 Hz source -> ~1245/605 Hz); RPM jitter 0.4% std at ~4 Hz rate, so h4 is ~7 Hz wide with a skirt. Steepest ~170 Hz/s.

descriptions.name: wide_fm_airshow
descriptions.description: Same physics, faster/closer (190 Hz base, h4 ~760 Hz source), 0.5% jitter, under an airshow announcer (continuous speech) and gusty wind.

descriptions.name: twin_props_a
descriptions.description: Twin-engine prop: two 3-blade families at 88 and 92.5 Hz (constant 4.5 Hz source offset), h1-6 each, shaft-rate sidebands (h*f0 +- f0/3) at -14 dB.

descriptions.name: twin_props_b
descriptions.description: Twin turboprop, 4-blade families at 102 and 108 Hz (6 Hz offset), sidebands -12 dB, lower pass with a ground reflection (R=0.5).

descriptions.name: dense_fan_a
descriptions.description: Crop-duster-like close low pass (60 m slant): f0 95 Hz, 20 lumpy harmonics to 1.9 kHz source; h20 sweeps ~450 Hz/s at CPA.

descriptions.name: dense_fan_b
descriptions.description: f0 82 Hz, 18 harmonics, 92 m slant, ground reflection (R=0.6) fades the tones.

descriptions.name: jet_a
descriptions.description: Jet flyover (292 m slant, 110 m/s): fan tone 1180 Hz plus compressor tones 1720/2350 Hz (0.3% N1 drift, in the truth) under a strong broadband roar, louder aft; ground reflection (R=0.8, mic 1.7 m) gives a moving Lloyd's-mirror comb. Truth = tones only.

descriptions.name: jet_b
descriptions.description: Low fast jet (117 m slant, 150 m/s): tones 1450/1950/2300 Hz source, roar 20 dB over the tones, R=0.9, mic 1.5 m.

descriptions.name: maneuver_parabola
descriptions.description: Curved track of the paper's eq. 42 shape, p(u) = (80u, 150 + 0.55u^2, 250) m: speed 80 -> 115 m/s, heading turns ~100 deg. Prop f0 105 Hz, 4 harmonics.

descriptions.name: maneuver_turn
descriptions.description: Constant-speed circling (r 700 m, 65 m/s, 68 s per orbit, nearest ~280 m) with a +3% throttle step at 70 s: approach/recede/approach, no straight template fits.

descriptions.name: speech_prop
descriptions.description: Prop pass (115 Hz, 4 harmonics, 400 m) under continuous two-talker speech whose voice harmonics cover the same band.

descriptions.name: wind_traffic_prop
descriptions.description: Prop pass (72 Hz, 5 harmonics, 500 m) with heavy gusty mic wind and distant road traffic (broadband 30-600 Hz roar + idle lines at 27/41 Hz).

descriptions.name: faint_long_a
descriptions.description: Distant high pass (1.6 km slant): f0 98 Hz, 3 harmonics, level set so the attacker's integrated z is ~5.

descriptions.name: faint_long_b
descriptions.description: Very distant pass (2.2 km), f0 130 Hz, 2 harmonics, with light speech; attacker z ~4.

descriptions.name: null_music
descriptions.description: Tonal music: chords, bass, melody with vibrato and glides, kick. No aircraft.

descriptions.name: null_birds
descriptions.description: Birdsong: FM sweeps (some down to 900 Hz), trills, a 450 Hz dove coo. No aircraft.

descriptions.name: null_traffic
descriptions.description: Distant road-traffic roar with idle engine lines, light wind. No aircraft.

descriptions.name: null_generator
descriptions.description: Stationary generator, 1800 rpm (30 Hz shaft) harmonics to 1.5 kHz with 0.8% governor drift (h45 wanders ~+-11 Hz), 50 Hz alternator lines. No aircraft.

descriptions.name: null_ambience
descriptions.description: Outdoor ambience only (pink floor + light wind). No aircraft.

descriptions.name: multipass_mixed
descriptions.description: Five aircraft in 8 min: single prop (350 m), twin (600 m, 5 Hz offset), jet (400 m, roar + ground comb) overlapped 20 s later by a second prop, close dense-fan prop (100 m), distant prop (1.2 km).

descriptions.name: multipass_speech
descriptions.description: Four aircraft under continuous two-talker speech for 7 min: prop (400 m), twin (500 m, 4 Hz offset), jet (350 m), and a circling prop (orbit r 600 m).

descriptions.name: multipass_faint
descriptions.description: Six passes in 10 min near the faint limit (attacker z ~3-10 each): distant props at 0.9-2.5 km, one twin, two of them overlapping, under ambience and light traffic.

findings:
Detector = base 37c5f34 (research/detection-v2 tip). The headline is **usable passes**: a pass
helps the geolocation attacker only through its steep CPA core.

**Per recording, usable passes before → after (oracle).** Single-pass clips: 12 aircraft
clips start with a usable pass. After cleaning, 10 still have one, and 2 clean
(maneuver_parabola, maneuver_turn). The oracle leaves 1 (wide_fm_airshow). Multi-pass:
multipass_mixed 6 → **3** (0); multipass_speech 4 → **3** (1); multipass_faint 1 → **1** (0).
With ≥ 2 usable passes left, both long recordings still geolocate with an unknown clock. The
oracle shows the remover can reach 0–1 everywhere: the gap is detection.

**What fails, by cause (core z after > 8 shows what the attacker keeps):**
1. **Jets: tones never detected** (jet_a, jet_b, and the jet passes in both multi-pass
   clips). Main-curve coverage is 0.02 / 0.14 and core coverage is 0. Fan/compressor tones
   at 1.1–1.8 kHz under a broadband roar and a moving Lloyd's-mirror comb produce no track
   (1 doppler track per clip). The cores stay usable (jet_a core z 30 → 30).
2. **Twin props: shaft-rate sidebands are never tracked.** The main families are covered
   1.00 at 3 Hz and their cores are removed. But the sidebands (h·f0 ± f0/3, −14 dB) keep
   core z 20–140 after. Some sidebands that were masked by the main lines (z ≤ 3 before) rise
   to z 5–12 once the lines are removed ("unmasked"). The oracle removes them (core z < 1),
   so this is detection, not removal.
3. **Dense fan: low harmonics' cores stay.** dense_fan_a h1/h2 are covered at 3 Hz, but only
   0.52 at 1 Hz in the core (the cores sweep up to 450 Hz/s), so the cores keep
   z 28 000 / 37 000. The same pattern appears in multipass_mixed pass 4 (h2 core z 1764,
   h3 439). The oracle reaches ≤ 2.
4. **Wide FM tone:** the whole curve is cleaned (z −0.8), but the h2 and h6 cores keep
   z 232 / 51 after (core coverage at 1 Hz 0.59). Under the announcer (wide_fm_airshow)
   coverage drops to 0.42 at 3 Hz and the plateaus also remain (curve z 25–27).
5. **Speech** (speech_prop, multipass_speech): coverage at 3 Hz is 0.32 / 0.25. Speech
   harmonics in the same band break the tracks.
6. **Faint / wind:** wind_traffic_prop, faint_long_a/b and 5 of 6 multipass_faint passes get
   no detection. Their curves are still visible to an integrating attacker (curve z 4–15),
   but the dechirped core z is < 5, so they are not usable: missing them costs nothing for
   geolocation.

**What passes:** curved tracks (parabola, turn: no straight template is needed by the
current tracker), single clean props (multipass_mixed pass 0), null_traffic and
null_ambience (0 corridors).

**False alarms on null clips:** null_generator has 57 doppler corridors, 897 s of tracks
(governor drift sweeps the 30 Hz harmonics; 25% of 40–450 Hz TF modified). null_music has 38
(399 s; 38% of 40–450 Hz modified; speech-band SNR 8 dB). null_birds has 17, all above
1 kHz. On aircraft clips 20–60% of doppler tracks follow no truth curve (twin_props_a: 107
of 186 tracks, 3418 s).

**Caveats.** The usable-pass rule is a proxy: a dechirped matched detector that knows the
true curve, which favours the attacker. Its thresholds come from noise-like null clips. The
real test is fc's (v, d) fit, and per-pass truth (v, d, h, f0) is in truth.json for that.
Tonal null clips (music, generator) give false "usable" z for random curves (p95 up to 18),
so the proxy should only be read on aircraft passes.
